Plompy Local 0.13.0Source guide · 2026-11-12

Documentation/Introduction

Your agent.
A little more reach.

Plompy Local connects an agent on your computer to selected tools running behind a local MCP endpoint. Your host client, such as Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode, plans the task and writes the response. Plompy handles the enabled integrations and local artifacts.

Plompy Local 0.13.0 ships as ready-made Docker images and a small starter kit. Download it, connect your preferred agent, and choose its tools. The Local images are separate from the Discord engine image. Check Compatibility and verification for what has actually been tested.

See what shipped in each release, including the current 0.13.0 Local images.

Pick your starting point#

  • Run locally with Docker: start the tools gateway, connect a client, and try a small task.
  • Research companies and draft messages: gather public evidence and save drafts without connecting a mailbox.
  • Use the existing Discord engine: let Plompy run a coding agent from your private Discord threads.

Two ways to use Plompy#

Plompy LocalDiscord engine
ConversationYour own MCP clientA private Discord thread
AgentCodex, Claude Code, OpenCode or another compatible clientThe runner selected by the engine
Plompy providesSelected tools and artifact storageQueue, runner sessions, memory and recovery
Model credentials in the containerNot requiredRequired by the selected runner
Discord configurationNot requiredRequired
Compose setupcompose.yaml from the Local starter kitcompose.yaml from the engine repository

The local gateway does not start a second model behind your host agent. It does not give Plompy access to every account or tool on your computer.

What stays with you#

Configuration, gateway credentials and generated files live in separate Docker volumes. You choose which integrations to enable. External search services and your model provider may receive task data when you use them. Read Permissions and data flow before connecting accounts.

No Plompy subscription or account is needed. Model access and third-party integrations may have their own charges.
